title: Signal Test Commons: a deterministic synthetic challenge suite for 512-channel signal monitors
description:
Signal Test Commons generates seeded, versioned challenges for evaluating 512-channel signal monitors offline. Frames are 16 x 32 grids of Gaussian noise with nine injected scenario types (stable noise, localized burst, block drift, global shock, weak burst, slow ramp, negative shift, variance change and baseline step), five episodes each, with channel-level ground truth. Predictions are scored as sets of channels, and two reference detectors (absolute threshold and robust z-score) give baselines. Each run writes a JSON report with the seed, challenge version, a SHA-256 of the frame values, scenario specifications and per-scenario metrics; multi-seed summaries report mean, minimum and maximum.

Scope: all data is SYNTHETIC, so results describe behaviour on this challenge only and do not indicate field performance. The reference detectors are baselines, not recommendations.

Usage: Python 3.10 or later, standard library only. Run python3 signal_test_commons.py --seed 7 --report challenge_report.json or python3 signal_test_commons.py --seeds 1-10. Tests: python3 -m unittest -v (run in CI on Python 3.10 to 3.13).

Citation: cite the concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23057992 for all versions, or the version DOI of the release you used. Source code: github.com/sparkainlp-x/signal-test-commons. Licence: AGPL-3.0-only; commercial licensing is available (see COMMERCIAL-LICENSE.md).
